newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish pound edges down vs stg after BoE report.
newsitem.headline: Irish pound edges down vs stg after BoE report.

text.p: The Irish pound edged lower against sterling in midday trade on Tuesday after the Bank of England called for a fresh rise in interest rates and warned British inflation was likely to overshoot without more policy action, dealers said.

Only last week rates were hiked to 6.25 percent from 6.00 percent in a bid to keep inflation in check. But in its first report since it was granted the freedom to set rates, the BoE warned inflation was likely to overshoot without policy action.

"As usual, we have been led by big international moves. In that regard, the most significant news surrounded the Bank of England report which has seen the punt weaken versus sterling," Austin Hughes, chief economist with Irish International Bank, said.

"We have a slightly less favourable outlook than we had at the end of last week when sterling was moving down. Perhaps the sell-off of sterling of last week was a bit exaggerated. But the weakness of the dollar puts a limit on what gains sterling might make," he added.

By 1300 GMT, the Irish pound eased to 0.9327 sterling from 0.9333 at Monday's close. The Irish unit eased down to 2.5747 marks from 2.5787 marks but edged up to $1.5144 from $1.5134 at the previous close.
Sterling was at 2.7625/35 marks compared to 2.7510/20 ahead of the BoE report and 2.7655/65 in late Europe on Monday. It was at $1.6233/45 compared to $1.6202/12 and $1.6230/40.
Dealers said the market was waiting for the release of U.S. April retail sales data at 1230 GMT for clues as to whether the Fed was likely to call for a change in rates when it next meets.
The forecast for U.S. retail sales is for a fall of 0.3 percent in April but for a rise of 0.1 percent year-on-year.
